correctness.rationale: The six and only factorizations with 1<=Omega(n)<=3 are p, p², pq, p³, p²q, pqr. Multiplicativity gives all claimed congruences exactly: for p prime σ(p)+φ(p)=2p; p² gives 2p²+1 mod3 so iff p!=3; pq gives 2(pq+1) mod4 so both odd; p³ gives 2p³+p+1 mod4 so p=1 mod4; p²q gives q(2p²+1)+2p+1 mod6 yielding q odd and (p=1 mod3 or p=3 and q=2 mod3); odd pqr has both σ,φ multiples of8, while 2qr divisibility mod8 iff q,r opposite mod4. Independent exact integer computation checked every 2<=n<=25000 with Omega<=3 against the six-shape criterion, 15,448 tested numbers (2,762+6,265+6,421), no counterexample. The unbounded theorem follows from shape exhaustion and modular algebra, not from this finite test.

Exhausting all six factorizations with Omega<=3 produces unbounded congruence families distinguishing primes, prime powers, semiprimes, and even versus odd three-prime products.
